verdicts.trueWording: (frequent AI users have historically done quite well identifying AI writing)
verdicts.note: Raw HTML of oneusefulthing.org/p/choosing-to-stay-human (curl, browser UA, 200) carries the quote word for word inside parentheses in the opening section; byline 'Ethan Mollick May 26, 2026' and datePublished 2026-05-26 match the attribution. The claim's 'at identifying' is its own connective; the page reads 'done quite well identifying'.

verdicts.trueWording: What makes AI imagery so lousy isn't the technology itself, but the cliche and superficial creative ambitions of those who use it
verdicts.note: Raw HTML of abcbranddesign.com (curl, 200) carries the cited quote 'AI image generation is essentially a truncated exercise in taste' verbatim, and two sentences earlier the sentence that supports every limb of the claim. Page bylines her as 'Elizabeth Goodspeed, US editor-at-large for "It's Nice That"'.

verdicts.trueWording: However, RLHF significantly reduces output diversity compared to SFT across a variety of measures
verdicts.note: arXiv PDF 2310.06452 (v3, 19 Feb 2024, 'Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2024') downloaded and text-extracted; the quote is verbatim in the Abstract. 'across their range of diversity metrics' = 'across a variety of measures'.

verdicts.trueWording: increasing the KL penalty coefficient leads to a drop in performance as expected, but also to a drop in per-input diversity, rather than a gain
verdicts.note: Section 6.3 'The Impact of the KL Penalty', p.9. Quote verbatim. The 'expected gain' limb is carried by the preceding sentences: the sweep was motivated by the hypothesis that a higher KL coefficient would keep the policy near SFT and so trade generalisation for diversity - 'The results show that this does not work'.

verdicts.trueWording: It is unclear whether this tradeoff is a fundamental one in fine-tuning LLMs with RLHF or just demonstrates a deficiency in current methods
verdicts.note: Section 7 Discussion and Conclusion, p.9. Quote verbatim and both disjuncts of the claim ('fundamental to RLHF fine-tuning' / 'a deficiency of current methods') are the paper's own two limbs.

verdicts.trueWording: For the diversity evaluations, we focus on the summarisation task specifically, as it has the most compelling results
verdicts.note: Section 6.2 Diversity, p.8. Quote verbatim. Precision note, not a defect in the claim: the reported diversity evaluation is summarisation-only, but the very next sentence records unreported initial diversity experiments on the instruction-following models (that is claim 744), so 'restricted' holds for what is presented rather than for what was ever run.

verdicts.trueWording: We ran some initial experiments evaluating diversity for the instruction-following models, but we did not see any meaningful differences
verdicts.note: Section 6.2 Diversity, p.8, immediately after the sentence verified at 743. Quote verbatim; the paper attributes the null result to metrics designed for short outputs and to RLHF's longer generations.

Table 11 (Appendix J.4, p.31) 'Per-input diversity scores for both RLHF and SFT models'. Columns run 125m/350m/1.3b/2.7b/6.7b, each split RLHF|SFT; the 6.7b pair on the EAD row is exactly 0.07 (RLHF) and 0.79 (SFT). Claim carries no quote string, so the check is the numeric row, which matches exactly.

verdicts.trueWording: For instance, in creative writing, VS increases diversity by 1.6-2.1x over direct prompting
verdicts.note: arXiv PDF 2510.01171, metadata /arXivID 'https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.01171v4' - the cited v4 exactly. Abstract carries the quote verbatim and, earlier in the same abstract, 'a simple, training-free prompting strategy', supporting the 'training-free' limb.

verdicts.trueWording: Our work shows that mode collapse can be mitigated at inference time
verdicts.note: Section 1, contribution 4 'Broader Implications for Alignment'. Quote verbatim within the sentence 'Our work shows that mode collapse can be mitigated at inference time, aligned models retain significant inherent diversity, and the quality-diversity trade-off can be systematically improved through prompting alone.'

verdicts.trueWording: aligned models retain significant inherent diversity
verdicts.note: Same sentence in Section 1 contribution 4 as 747. Quote verbatim.

verdicts.trueWording: we first study three creative writing tasks: poem continuation, story generation, and joke writing
verdicts.note: Section 5 Creative Writing, 'Benchmarks' paragraph. Quote verbatim; poems from PoemHunter.com, stories from BookMIA, jokes from 100 curated r/DadJokes prompts.

Figure 3a, 'Average semantic diversity scores (%) in poem (a)', bar labels in method order Direct, CoT, Sequence, Multi-turn, VS-Standard, VS-CoT, VS-Multi: Direct 11.4, VS-Standard 21.9, VS-CoT 25.8 - exactly as claimed. Section 5.1 confirms these are semantic diversity scores averaged across models. No quote string on the claim; the numeric check is exact.

Table 2 caption 'Human-rated diversity (1 = Very Similar, 4 = Very Dissimilar)'; poem row Direct 1.90, VS-Standard 2.39. Section 5.2 text: 'We recruited 90 annotators (30 per task) to evaluate 90 output pairs per task on 4-point Likert scales', and Appendix E.3 repeats 'a four-point Likert scale'. Every limb - 90 annotators, poem, 2.39 vs 1.90, four-point scale - is exact.

verdicts.trueWording: We observe an emergent trend where larger models benefit more from VS
verdicts.note: Section 5.1 'Emergent Trend' paragraph carries the quote verbatim; the Figure 3 caption repeats 'e-f: Emergent Trend where larger models benefit more from VS'. Section 5.1 quantifies it: large models (GPT-4.1, Gemini-2.5-Pro) gain 1.5 to 2 times more diversity than small ones.
